title: 那只“害羞”的气球
title_en: The Balloon That Was Too Shy to Pop
summary_zh: 化学社去小学表演科学秀，压轴的氢气球却怎么也不爆。负责的大学生没有慌，反而把失败变成了全场最难忘的一课。读完你会学到讲故事的地道表达和“与过去事实相反”的虚拟语气。
body: Every spring, the chemistry society takes a science show to a local primary school, and this year Priya had been put in charge of the finale. She had spent weeks devising it: a hydrogen balloon, touched with a candle on a long stick, would vanish in a flash of light. The trouble started in the car park. The gas cylinder had the wrong valve, and by the time someone had fixed it, the hall was already full of restless children. Then came a second complication, because the head teacher, who had seen the word 'explosion' in the email the society used to advertise the show, asked them to use a much smaller balloon. Priya's hands were shaking as she lifted the stick. The little balloon refused to pop; the candle had gone out on the way up, leaving her standing there with a smoking stick and every face in the hall staring at her. It was the most challenging thirty seconds of her degree. Instead of panicking, she turned to the children and asked why they thought it hadn't worked. A girl in the front row put up her hand and suggested, quite seriously, that the balloon was shy. Everyone laughed, Priya relit the candle, and this time it burst with a sharp crack and a brief orange glow that made the whole room gasp. After the show, a teacher told her that if it had worked first time, the children would have forgotten it by lunch. Her inability to get it right at once had turned an ordinary demonstration into a smash hit, because it showed the pupils that scientists get things wrong too. The school later sent a shiny certificate, but the society's most beloved souvenir is a child's drawing of a very shy balloon.

questions.prompt: According to the story, why did the failed first attempt turn out to be a good thing?
options: It meant the show could finish earlier than planned
It showed the children that scientists also make mistakes
It gave the girl in the front row a chance to perform
It proved that the smaller balloon was the safer choice
questions.evidence: because it showed the pupils that scientists get things wrong too

questions.prompt: What does 'a smash hit' mean near the end of the story?
options: A loud accident that frightened the children
A piece of equipment that got broken
A great success that everyone enjoyed
A mistake the society wanted to forget
questions.evidence: had turned an ordinary demonstration into a smash hit

questions.prompt: Why did the head teacher most likely ask for a much smaller balloon?
options: The hall was too small for a big one
She thought big balloons were boring
She wanted to save the society money
She was worried the demonstration might be dangerous
questions.evidence: who had seen the word 'explosion' in the email the society used to advertise the show

questions.prompt: What did the girl in the front row suggest?
options: That they had used the wrong gas
That they should try again after lunch
That the balloon was shy
That the candle was too small
questions.evidence: suggested, quite seriously, that the balloon was shy

vocabulary.meaning: 压轴节目；最后一个环节
vocabulary.example: The fireworks were the finale of the whole festival.

vocabulary.meaning: 设计；构思（新办法、新方案）
vocabulary.example: She spent the summer devising a new timetable for the club.
The children grew restless after an hour in the car.

vocabulary.meaning: 新麻烦；让事情更复杂的情况
vocabulary.example: The trip went smoothly until a complication at the airport.
His inability to say no means he is always too busy.

expressions.note: be put in charge of sth：被委派负责某事，常用于活动、项目分工。
讲故事的常用开头，一下子制造悬念：The trouble started when…
后接从句，强调“来不及了”：By the time we arrived, the film had started.
put up your hand 是英式课堂说法，和 raise your hand 意思一样。
英式口语，first time 前不加 the 也不加 for，相当于 on the first try。
口语，语气轻松，常用来安慰人：Everyone gets things wrong sometimes.

knowledge.quote: if it had worked first time, the children would have forgotten it by lunch
knowledge.explanation: 与过去事实相反：if + had done，主句 would have done。事实是第一次没成功，所以孩子们反而记住了。

knowledge.quote: leaving her standing there with a smoking stick and every face in the hall staring at her
knowledge.explanation: 现在分词 leaving 引出前一句造成的结果；standing、staring 也是现在分词，描写当时的尴尬画面。

knowledge.quote: the head teacher, who had seen the word 'explosion' in the email the society used to advertise the show, asked them to use a much smaller balloon
knowledge.explanation: 非限制性定语从句 who had seen… 补充校长为什么担心；the email (that) the society used… 省略了关系词。

speaking: 用 1 分钟讲一次你当众“出糗”却意外收获好结果的经历，用上 The trouble started… 和一个 if it had…, … would have… 的句子。
writing: 用 150–200 词写一个小故事：一次活动或展示出了意外，你是怎么救场的。至少用一个现在分词短语（如 leaving me…）和 by the time。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 if it had…, … would have… 说一件因为“没一次成功”反而更好的事。
task.model: if it had worked first time, the children would have forgotten it by lunch

title: 迎新集市上的天文社
title_en: Come for the Sweets, Stay for the Comet
summary_zh: 迎新集市上，天文社的摊位无人问津，隔壁攀岩社却排起了长队。两位社员商量怎样用社团独有的天文台圆顶吸引新人。读完你会学到被拒绝时互相打气、出点子和分工的地道口语。
body: Hana: Twenty people have walked past our stall in the last ten minutes, and not one of them has stopped. Tom: Don't take it personally, because rejection is basically the whole job at a freshers' fair. Hana: That's easy for you to say, but the climbing club next door has a queue, and all they've got is a shiny poster and free sweets. Tom: Then let's advertise the one thing nobody else in this hall can offer, which is the dome. Hana: You mean the observatory above the physics labs? I thought it was closed after the suspension of the rooftop sessions last year. Tom: It was, but it reopened over the summer, and we're the only society with a key. Hana: That's exciting, so why on earth isn't it on our banner? Tom: Because whoever made the banner spelled 'astronomy' wrong, and nobody's had time to make a new one. Hana: Forget the banner: we've accumulated a few hundred followers who never hear from us, so I'll post a photo of the telescope tonight. Tom: Good, and mention the legendary night when half the campus queued on the stairs to see a comet. Hana: Wait, was that real, or just a story the committee tells new members? Tom: Completely real: people still remember it hanging like a faint glow above the crown of the big oak by the library. Hana: So the pitch is simple: come for the sweets, stay for the comet. Tom: Except we don't have any sweets. Hana: Then I'll buy some, because our motto is literally 'Strive for the stars', and I refuse to lose to a climbing wall. Tom: While you're gone, I'll do a solo shift and try smiling at people. Hana: Try shouting 'free telescope' instead; it'll work better than your smile.

questions.prompt: What does Tom think will make their society stand out?
options: Free sweets like the ones the climbing club offers
Access to an observatory that no other society has
A new banner with the correct spelling
The large number of followers they already have
questions.evidence: let's advertise the one thing nobody else in this hall can offer, which is the dome

questions.prompt: Why did Hana think the observatory might not be available?
options: The banner said that it was closed
The physics department had lost the key
The rooftop sessions had been stopped the year before
The telescope had been damaged over the summer
questions.evidence: I thought it was closed after the suspension of the rooftop sessions last year

questions.prompt: What does Hana mean by "come for the sweets, stay for the comet"?
options: People should leave once the sweets are gone
A comet can be seen every week
Small treats will attract people, and the observatory will keep them interested
The society only offers sweets
questions.evidence: So the pitch is simple: come for the sweets, stay for the comet.

questions.prompt: What does "accumulated" mean in "we've accumulated a few hundred followers"?
options: blocked
gradually collected
lost
paid
questions.evidence: we've accumulated a few hundred followers who never hear from us

vocabulary.example: Every writer has to learn to live with rejection.
We watched the moon through the telescope at the observatory.
Over the years she has accumulated hundreds of old postcards.

vocabulary.meaning: 传奇般的；（在某圈子里）出了名的
vocabulary.example: Our coach's terrible jokes are legendary in the team.
They hung a banner across the gate to welcome the new students.

expressions.note: 安慰别人：被拒绝、被批评并不是针对你这个人。也可以说 It's nothing personal.

expressions.text: That's easy for you to say
expressions.note: 略带不服气，表示对方没处在你的处境，朋友之间常用。
on earth 放在疑问词后加强语气，表示惊讶或想不通。

expressions.text: come for the sweets, stay for the comet
expressions.note: come for X, stay for Y 是宣传常用句式：先用小东西吸引人，再用真正的亮点留住人。
解释事情为什么还没做，口语里常用现在完成时的缩写。
交代对方离开期间自己做什么，从句用现在时表示将来。

knowledge.quote: Twenty people have walked past our stall in the last ten minutes
knowledge.explanation: 现在完成时 + in the last ten minutes：从十分钟前一直到现在的累计结果，抱怨“到目前为止”的情况时很好用。

knowledge.quote: whoever made the banner spelled 'astronomy' wrong
knowledge.explanation: whoever made the banner 是名词性从句，作整句的主语，意思是“不管是谁做的横幅”，不知道或不想点名时用。

knowledge.quote: I'll do a solo shift and try smiling at people
knowledge.explanation: try doing 表示“试着做一下看效果如何”；try to do 则是“努力去做（不一定做得到）”。

speaking: 和同伴模拟：你们在迎新集市为一个社团招新。用 1 分钟说出你们社团最独特的卖点，用上 come for…, stay for… 和 Don't take it personally。
writing: 用 120–180 词为你喜欢的一个社团写一段招新文案，突出一个别人没有的亮点，并至少用一个现在完成时句子。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 come for…, stay for… 为你熟悉的一个地方或活动写一句宣传语。
task.model: come for the sweets, stay for the comet

title: 申请休学一学期
title_en: Asking to Pause My Degree for a Term
summary_zh: 父亲手术后需要休养，家里的农场又正赶上产羔季，大学生 Sam 给导师写信申请休学一学期。这封邮件示范了怎样把为难的私事讲清楚、讲得体。读完你会学到正式邮件中提出请求、说明理由的表达。
body: Dear Dr Okafor, I am writing to ask whether I could take a suspension of studies for the spring term, and to explain why I have missed your seminars over the last fortnight. My father had a kidney operation three weeks ago, and although it went well, a minor complication has slowed the healing, so he will need several more weeks of rest. Our family runs a small sheep farm, and his inability to work at this time of year is a real problem. The lambs are due soon, and farming does not stop for anyone's recovery. My mother has asked me to come home and help until he is back on his feet. If the suspension is approved, I understand that my completion date will move back by a term, and I am prepared to accept that. I have already retrieved my draft essays from the shared drive, so I can keep reading in the evenings without falling too far behind. You once told our group that a mature decision is often the one that sounds less impressive. I would rather pause properly now than strive to do both and manage neither. My father, who studied here himself and still talks about the place with great affection, was the one who persuaded me to ask for a suspension instead of simply dropping out. The university has been an anchor for me since my first year, and I fully intend to come back in the autumn. Could you let me know which forms I need to complete, and whether we could speak briefly on the phone this week? Best wishes, Sam Turner

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Sam's email?
options: To complain about the way the seminars are organised
To ask for an extension on one late essay
To tell his tutor that he is leaving university for good
To ask for a term away from his studies and explain why
questions.evidence: I am writing to ask whether I could take a suspension of studies for the spring term

questions.prompt: Why is Sam's help needed at home right now?
options: His father cannot work during a busy time on the farm
His mother has also had an operation
The family has decided to sell the farm
His father wants him to take over the farm permanently
questions.evidence: his inability to work at this time of year is a real problem

questions.prompt: Why does Sam mention Dr Okafor's remark about "a mature decision"?
options: To prove that he has finished his essays
To ask for a better grade
To complain about the course
To show that pausing is sensible even if it sounds less impressive
questions.evidence: a mature decision is often the one that sounds less impressive

questions.prompt: What does "complication" mean in "a minor complication has slowed the healing"?
options: a successful result
a type of medicine
a problem that makes a situation more difficult
a hospital form
questions.evidence: a minor complication has slowed the healing

vocabulary.example: She applied for a suspension of studies after her daughter was born.
I finally retrieved my umbrella from the lost property office.
It was a very mature response from someone so young.
He still speaks about his old school with real affection.

vocabulary.meaning: 精神支柱；让人安心的依靠
vocabulary.example: During those difficult years, music was my anchor.

expressions.text: I am writing to ask whether
expressions.note: 正式邮件的标准开头，开门见山说明目的，比 I want to ask 得体得多。
解释季节性原因时常用，如 The roads are busy at this time of year.
be / get back on one's feet：可指身体康复，也可指经济、生意恢复。
move back 指把日期往后推；by 表示推迟的幅度，如 by two weeks。
fall behind 落后；too far behind 强调差距大，学习、工作都常用。
drop out (of university) 指没读完就离开，是口语也是正式说法。

knowledge.quote: If the suspension is approved, I understand that my completion date will move back by a term
knowledge.explanation: 真实条件句：if + 一般现在时（这里是被动 is approved），主句谈将来的结果。主动说明后果，显得考虑周全。

knowledge.quote: My father, who studied here himself and still talks about the place with great affection, was the one who persuaded me to ask for a suspension instead of simply dropping out.
knowledge.explanation: 第一个 who 引导非限制性定语从句，补充父亲的背景；the one who… 是限制性定语从句，强调“正是他”。

knowledge.quote: I am writing to ask whether I could take a suspension of studies for the spring term, and to explain why I have missed your seminars over the last fortnight.
knowledge.explanation: 两个不定式 to ask… and to explain… 并列表示写信目的；could 让请求更委婉。

speaking: 用 1 分钟向老师口头说明：你因为家里有事需要请假一周。说清原因和补救计划，并用上 at this time of year 或 back on (his/her) feet。
writing: 用 150–200 词给导师写一封邮件，申请推迟某项作业或请假。说明原因、提出具体请求，并至少用一个 If…, … will… 的条件句。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 If… is approved, I understand that… 写一句申请时主动说明后果的话。
task.model: If the suspension is approved, I understand that my completion date will move back by a term

title: 文献评析不是吐槽
title_en: How to Critique an Article Without Just Complaining
summary_zh: 很多课程都要求写 critique（文献评析），但它不是“摘要加几句吐槽”。这篇指南一步步讲怎样提取论点、设计检验问题、用原文支撑判断。读完你会学到学术评析中常用的动词和句式。
body: Sooner or later, most courses ask you to write a critique of a published article, and the first attempt is usually more challenging than students expect. A critique is not a summary with a few complaints at the end; it is an argument about how well the article does what it sets out to do. Read the piece once without taking notes, simply to understand its main claim. On the second reading, extract the parts that carry the argument, such as the research question, the method, the key evidence and the conclusion. Copy them into a simple table rather than highlighting whole pages, because a highlighted page is surprisingly hard to retrieve anything from a week later. Next, devise three or four questions to test the article against, such as whether the method suits the question and whether the evidence really supports the conclusion. Imagine an article arguing that hydrogen will soon power most city buses. A weak critique would simply call the author too optimistic, whereas a strong one would point to the exact step where the reasoning goes further than the evidence allows. Anchor every judgement in a specific page or quotation, so that your reader can check it. Avoid words that merely evoke a feeling, such as 'brilliant' or 'disappointing', unless you explain exactly why. As your notes accumulate, resist the temptation to include everything you noticed, and develop the two or three points that matter most. Saying clearly what an article does well shows that you have read it fairly, neither as a loyal follower of the author nor as an enemy hunting for mistakes. Finally, leave a day between the completion of your draft and your final edit, because you will notice weaknesses that you were too close to see.

questions.prompt: According to the guide, how is a critique different from a summary?
options: It is shorter and leaves out the method
It judges how well the article achieves its aims
It focuses only on the mistakes the author made
It repeats the conclusion in the student's own words
questions.evidence: it is an argument about how well the article does what it sets out to do

questions.prompt: Why does the guide recommend copying key parts into a table?
options: Tables look more professional to markers
Highlighting is not allowed in library books
Tables make it easier to quote the author's exact words
Information on a highlighted page is hard to find again later
questions.evidence: because a highlighted page is surprisingly hard to retrieve anything from a week later

questions.prompt: What does the example of the hydrogen buses show about a strong critique?
options: It agrees with the author on every point
It uses stronger adjectives than a weak one
It points to exactly where the reasoning goes beyond the evidence
It is mainly about transport
questions.evidence: a strong one would point to the exact step where the reasoning goes further than the evidence allows

questions.prompt: What does "evoke" mean in "words that merely evoke a feeling"?
options: hide
measure
explain
bring to mind or call up
questions.evidence: Avoid words that merely evoke a feeling

vocabulary.example: Our first assignment is a critique of a short research paper.
Try to extract the three main ideas from each chapter.
The teacher asked us to devise our own experiment.
Always anchor your opinion in a real example.
Dust and old papers accumulate quickly on my desk.

expressions.note: 放句首，表示某事早晚会发生，语气自然，口语书面都常用。

expressions.meaning: 本来打算做到；着手去做
expressions.note: what the article sets out to do = 文章自己声称要完成的目标，评价作品时很常用。
point to sth：指出、援引（证据或问题），比 say 更有分量。
后接动词原形，给建议时很地道：Resist the temptation to check your phone.
hunt for sth：到处搜寻，hunting for mistakes 带一点“鸡蛋里挑骨头”的意味。

expressions.meaning: 离得太近反而看不清；当局者迷
expressions.note: be too close to sth：身在其中，难以客观判断。

knowledge.quote: Imagine an article arguing that hydrogen will soon power most city buses.
knowledge.explanation: 现在分词短语 arguing that… 作后置定语修饰 article，相当于 an article which argues that…，学术写作中很常见。

knowledge.quote: Saying clearly what an article does well shows that you have read it fairly
knowledge.explanation: 动名词短语 Saying clearly what an article does well 作主语，谓语用单数 shows。

knowledge.quote: As your notes accumulate, resist the temptation to include everything you noticed
knowledge.explanation: as 引导时间状语从句，意为“随着……”，表示两件事同步变化；主句是祈使句，直接给建议。

speaking: 用 1 分钟评价你最近读过的一篇文章或一本书：先说它想做到什么（sets out to），再指出一个优点和一个不足（point to…）。
writing: 用 180–220 词写一段评析：选一篇你读过的文章，说明它的主要观点、一个有力之处和一个薄弱环节，并至少用一个动名词短语作主语。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 As…, resist the temptation to… 给同学一条学习建议。
task.model: As your notes accumulate, resist the temptation to include everything you noticed
